boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten distinct campus study environments, from general library seating to media, language, and special-collection research spaces.

cards.title: McCabe Library
cards.subtitle: Humanities and social sciences library
cards.notes: Set up with course materials or a research plan; McCabe is Swarthmore’s humanities and social sciences library and offers varied study-space formats.
cards.short_summary: A general-purpose library setting with individual, open-table, and group-study options.
cards.evidence_claim: Swarthmore identifies McCabe as its humanities and social sciences library; its libraries provide individual carrels, open tables, and group study rooms.
cards.access_notes: Use the Libraries site or service desk to confirm current building hours and visitor access before going.

cards.title: Cornell Science Library
cards.subtitle: Science Center
cards.notes: Bring science or engineering work that benefits from nearby subject collections, then ask the science librarian for research help during weekday hours.
cards.short_summary: A Science Center library supporting undergraduate science and engineering research.
cards.evidence_claim: Cornell Library of Science & Engineering is in the Science Center, supports undergraduate science and engineering research, and has a science librarian available on weekdays.
cards.access_notes: Confirm Cornell’s current hours and any access requirements on the library page before visiting.

cards.title: Underhill Music and Dance Library
cards.subtitle: Lang Music Building
cards.notes: Use this setting for music or dance research when listening, viewing, or score-based materials can support the work you are doing.
cards.short_summary: A performing-arts library within the College’s three main campus libraries.
cards.evidence_claim: Swarthmore lists Underhill Music and Dance Library as one of its three main libraries, whose study spaces include carrels, open tables, and group study rooms.
cards.access_notes: Check current library hours and access policies before visiting the Lang Music Building.

cards.entity_name: Frank and Vera Brown Color Room
cards.title: Frank and Vera Brown Color Room
cards.subtitle: McCabe Library
cards.notes: Plan a color-focused project or discussion here; the room combines pigment samples, physics experiments, and a color-book collection.
cards.short_summary: A McCabe study room designed around interdisciplinary investigation of color.
cards.evidence_claim: The Color Room in McCabe contains pigment samples, physics experiments, and a rare and circulating book collection on color.
cards.source_title: Swarthmore College Libraries: ACRL Excellence Award application
cards.access_notes: This is a specialized study room; ask library staff about present availability and any reservation procedure.

cards.title: Language Center
cards.subtitle: Temporarily Science Center 238
cards.notes: Use the center for language, literature, film, media, arts, or culture coursework; email the center first to confirm available resources.
cards.short_summary: A flexible learning space supporting language and media-oriented study.
cards.evidence_claim: Swarthmore describes the Language Center as a flexible learning space supporting study of foreign language, literature, film, media, arts, and culture; it is temporarily in Science Center 238.
cards.source_title: Language Center and Creative Media Commons
cards.access_notes: The College notes a temporary location; contact lmc@swarthmore.edu for current resources and access details.

cards.title: Creative Media Commons
cards.subtitle: First floor, Martin Hall
cards.notes: Bring a media-based assignment and use the commons for supported work; it has a recording space and expertise for media production tasks.
cards.short_summary: A Martin Hall setting for creative and technical media coursework.
cards.evidence_claim: Swarthmore reports that the Creative Media Commons is on Martin Hall’s first floor and offers media-work help plus a recording space.
cards.access_notes: Check with the Creative Media Commons for current workstation, recording-space, equipment, and support availability.

cards.title: Black Cultural Center Library
cards.subtitle: Black Cultural Center
cards.notes: Search the Tripod catalog before heading over, then focus your reading or project work around this smaller campus library collection.
cards.short_summary: A specialized campus library collection in the Black Cultural Center.
cards.evidence_claim: Swarthmore’s instructional-staff handbook identifies a small library collection in the Black Cultural Center.
cards.access_notes: Confirm current building access and collection availability with the College before visiting.

cards.title: Beit Midrash
cards.subtitle: Lodge 5 near Bond Hall
cards.notes: Use this text-study library for focused reading on Judaism, Jewish history, or culture, and check in before using the space for coursework.
cards.short_summary: A Jewish text-study library and specialized campus collection.
cards.evidence_claim: The Beit Midrash in Lodge 5 is a Jewish text-study library used for Jewish studies classes and weekly text study.
cards.access_notes: The space hosts classes and programming; verify access and quiet-use expectations with Swarthmore Kehilah or the Religion Department.

cards.title: Friends Historical Library
cards.subtitle: McCabe Library
cards.notes: Come with a defined Quaker-history question, then consult staff about relevant manuscripts, books, pamphlets, pictures, and research procedures.
cards.short_summary: A McCabe-based special collection for research in Quaker history and related records.
cards.evidence_claim: Swarthmore lists Friends Historical Library among its special collections and identifies it as a Quaker collection and College archives resource.
cards.access_notes: Special-collection use can involve distinct reading-room procedures; contact Friends Historical Library before a research visit.

cards.title: Peace Collection Reading Room
cards.subtitle: McCabe Library
cards.notes: Search the finding aids and catalog first, then visit the reading room for primary-source research on peace and nonviolent social change.
cards.short_summary: An in-person research setting for the Peace Collection’s archival materials.
cards.evidence_claim: Swarthmore says most Peace Collection materials are not digitized and must be consulted in person in the Reading Room.
cards.access_notes: Review catalog records and contact the Peace Collection ahead of time for current Reading Room access and collection limitations.
